recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if resource page generation stops surfacing the root StructureDefinition definition or if the Security WG explicitly wants a new editorial change to duplicate the clinical-significance wording in the narrative introduction.
issue_request: FHIR-5392 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 Security ballot issue asking to replace the original narrow Provenance wording with W3C PROV language and to clarify that provenance statements can indicate clinical significance for authenticity, reliability, trustworthiness, integrity, and lifecycle stage.
initial_application: Historical commit 5c0d5519e3 changed the Provenance spreadsheet root definition from the old creation-focused wording to the approved FHIR-5392 wording. The later XML StructureDefinition conversion preserved that wording in the resource description and root element definition.
additional_context: Provenance is active in the current build through source/fhir.ini. A later Security WG commit revised the separate narrative introduction to a shorter scope summary, but it does not contradict the authoritative root definition. No relevant Zulip or Confluence evidence was found that changes the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The build-scope StructureDefinition already conveys the requested definition and clinical-significance semantics, and duplicating the same text in narrative prose would be editorial redundancy rather than a required correction.
